description: Pinned standard web benchmarks for Vulpra Simulator benchmark gates. Sources are immutable upstream codeload tarballs (fixed commit + SHA-256); Tools/CI/benchmark-fixture.py downloads, verifies, and serves them same-origin with a score-reporting runner page. Scores are captured from the page title (GeckoView:PageTitleChanged -> 'Engine title: ...' log line) so no JS injection channel is required.

device.reason: Native iPad app (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY=1,2); portrait 1024x1366 satisfies the Speedometer 3.1 850x650 minimum viewport without headless rotation. MotionMark's landscape-only Start button is never enabled in portrait, so the same-origin runner waits for benchmarkController.frameRateDetectionComplete (FPS detection always completes, even on failure) and then calls benchmarkController.startBenchmark() directly — no landscape required.

benchmarks.purpose: Web application responsiveness (simulated user interaction timing)
benchmarks.notes: First-pass Simulator gate on the JIT-disabled v5 engine. A single iteration of the full default suite (20 suites / 58 subtests) does not complete within CI budget in interpreter mode (observed: still running after 2h15m on the macOS runner with iterationCount=1), so this gate runs an explicit representative subset via suites= (TodoMVC-JavaScript-ES5, Editor-CodeMirror, Charts-chartjs, Perf-Dashboard; 4 suites / 11 subtests) at iterationCount=1. The reported #result-number score is the Speedometer geomean of this subset only and is NOT comparable to the official full-suite Speedometer score; it is a stable same-engine regression proxy. Restore the full default suite (drop the suites= param) and iterationCount=10 together with a JIT-enabled engine, then re-baseline. timeoutSeconds=3600 is the wall-clock budget for the interpreter-mode subset run; the runner page also publishes progress lines ('Engine title: VulpraBenchmark speedometer3 progress=...') so a slow or stalled suite is visible in the evidence log.

benchmarks.purpose: Graphics and animation frame-rate (canvas rendering at target fps)
JavaScript and WebAssembly throughput (geometric mean of benchmark scores)
benchmarks.notes: JetStream 3.0 default suite includes ~12 WebAssembly workloads (tsf-wasm, richards-wasm, sqlite3-wasm, 8bitbench-wasm, zlib-wasm, dotnet-interp/aot-wasm, j2cl-box2d-wasm, Dart-flute-todomvc-wasm, Kotlin-compose-wasm, transformersjs-bert-wasm, argon2-wasm, gcc-loops-wasm, quicksort-wasm, HashSet-wasm); the driver aborts the whole run when any sub-benchmark throws (JetStreamDriver.js start(): catch -> reportError -> throw e), and the page refuses a partial suite. The current v5 engine calls JS::DisableJitBackend() in every Gecko child process (toolkit/xre/IOSBootstrap.mm ChildProcessInitImpl), setting JitOptions.disableJitBackend=true, so wasm::HasSupport() is false (HasPlatformSupport -> HasJitBackend -> !disableJitBackend) and WebAssembly is unavailable. Therefore the full JetStream 3.0 gate is guaranteed to fail on the JIT-disabled engine: requiresJitBackend=true and enabledByDefault=false, and the benchmark workflow refuses to select it. Re-enable only together with a JIT-enabled engine build.
